REPORT 
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action T aken by the Government on 
the observations/recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred and Nineteenth Report on 
Demands for Grants 2015-16 of the Ministry of Cultu re which was presented to both the 
Houses of Parliament on 28 th  April, 2015. 
2.  Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 19 th  August, 2015, in respect 
of all the observations/recommendations contained i n the Report. The replies have been 
categorized as follows:– 
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government: 
Paragraph Nos. 13,16, 20,27, 31,34,36,38,39,40, 42,  43,44, 46, 50,51,52, 55,56,57, 62, 64, 
65,66,67,68, 74, 76, 79, 80, 81,83,85,87, 91,94, 97 ,98,101,106,108, 110, 112,114, 
116,117,118,123,124,127,129, 131,132,134, & 136      Total:55 
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of 
the Government replies:– 
Paragraph Nos.53& 99         Total:2 
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich replies of the Government have not 
been accepted by the Committee: 
Paragraph Nos. : 48, 95 &96        Total:3 
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of whi ch final replies of the Government are 
still awaited. 
Paragraph Nos: 54 & 75         Total:2 
3. The Committee desires that final replies in resp ect of those recommendations/observations 
which have been categorized as interim replies by t he Committee should be furnished at the 
earliest. 
4.  On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Co mmittee has made observations on 
each item of Action Taken/proposed to be taken by t he concerned Ministries. The 
recommendations of the Committee contained in the T wo Hundred and Nineteenth Report, 
action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommenda tions/observations of the Committee on 
each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs: 
 
Assessment of the Demands for Grants (2015-16) of the Ministry 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
5.     The Committee notes that the present Budget Estima tes shows an increase of just 
Rs.10 crores in comparison to the Revised Estimate last year i.e.,  (2014-15). The Committee 
is also surprised to note that the Ministry had to face a sharp budgetary cut at RE stage in the 
last financial year. The Committee failed to get a convincing reason for this cut. Given the 
importance of the mandate of this Ministry i.e,  to preserve, protect and promote our vast 
cultural heritage, both tangible and intangible, sp read across the length and breadth of the 
country, the Committee is at a loss to see that Pla n allocation to this Ministry has come down 
from Rs.1835 crore in BE 2014-15 to Rs.1500 crore i n RE 2014-15 and to Rs.1455 crore in 
BE of 2015-16. Such allocation are highly insuffici ent and the Committee recommends that 
Plan allocation for the Department be increased adequately at RE stage.       
          (Recommendation at Para No.13 of the 219 
th  Report) 

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
6.  As against total budgetary provision of Rs. 251 1.00 crore at BE 2014-15 which was 
reduced to Rs. 2159.00 crore at RE 2014-15, the bud get for 2015-16 for Ministry of Culture 
has been pegged at Rs. 2169.00 crore consisting of Rs. 1455.00 crore for Plan and Rs. 714.00 
crore under Non-Plan Heads. This budget is almost equal or about 0.46% more than budgetary 
provisions at RE 2014-15. Ministry of Finance has n ot intimated any reason for the reduction 
in Annual Plan allocation at RE stage during 2014-1 5. However, the Ministry will make 
efforts to seek an additional allocation at RE stage during the current financial year 2015-16. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
7.   The Committee desires to be apprised of the effor ts made by the Ministry to 
seek additional allocation at RE stage during 2015-16 and the outcome thereof. 
Twelfth Five Year Plan 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
8.  The Committee notes that against the proposed outla y of Rs.18608.94 crore, only 
Rs.7275.00 crore were earmarked for the 12 
th  Five Year Plan. Due to this severe downsizing, 
many important Schemes mentioned above, could not be taken up by the Ministry. Since three 
years of the plan period have been over, the Commit tee recommends that for the remaining 
two years, the Plan allocation for the Ministry of Culture should be hiked so that important 
schemes/projects should not suffer. The Committee a lso would like to know the rationale for 
abandoning the three schemes in the Museum Sector b y the Ministry along with an impact-
assessment Report.  
                                       (Para No. 16  of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
9.  Against the proposed outlay of Rs. 18668.94 cro re for the 12
th  Five Year Plan 
(2012-2017), Planning Commission had approved a Pla n allocation of Rs. 7275.00 crore for 
the Ministry for various priority areas, new scheme s, perspectives and ongoing 
schemes/activities/projects under different sectors. As per 12 th  Plan proposals submitted to the 
Planning Commission, various new schemes under diff erent sectors viz. Promotion of Art & 
Culture, Archaeology, Museum, Public Library, Buddh ist & Tibetan Institution Sectors were 
proposed with sufficient outlay included under proposed total outlay of Rs. 18668.94 crore for 
the 12 th  Plan. Since, Planning Commission has approved only  Rs. 7275.00 crore for the 12 th  
Five Year Plan which is about 38.97% of the propose d outlay, many programmes /schemes 
proposed in the 12 th  Plan have not been taken up to avoid their spread of finances on account 
of reduced allocation of Plan funds for the Ministr y. This is the main reason/rationale for not 
initiating some of the schemes under Museum and Promotion of Art & Culture Sectors. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
10.  The Committee notes the reply. The Committee hopes  that the enhanced 
allocation at RE stage would enable the Ministry to allocate funds for important schemes 
which are presently held up for want of funds. The Ministry may also furnish an impact 
assessment Report on non-initiation of certain sche mes under Museum and Promotion 
of Art & Culture Sectors. 
Spending pattern during the Twelfth Plan 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
11.  The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry wa s able to spend more than 90% 

of its allocation during the first three years of t he Twelfth Plan. At the same time, the 
Committee observes that better planning and supervi sion could have definitely improved the 
pace of utilization.           
               (Para No. 20 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
12. The trend of Plan expenditure during 12 
th  Plan period shows the gradual increase as 
per position indicated in the following table: 
 (Rs. in crore) 
Year BE RE AE % Actual w.r.t. RE  
12 th  Plan 7275.00    
2012-13 864.00 864.00 803.70 93.03 
2013-14 1537.00 1470.00 1380.13 93.89 
2014-15 1835.00 1500.00 1418.76* 94.58 
2015-16 1455.00    
2016-17     
*Provisional, subject to revision.  
  For better planning and supervision to enhance th e pace of Plan expenditure during 
2015-16, all the cultural organizations and other c oncerned offices have been advised by 
Secretary (Culture), to take every possible step to  ensure that underutilization of funds does 
not occur and bring bottlenecks, if any, in incurring expenditure, to his notice. These measures 
are expected to show better and improved results in  spending Plan funds to the optimal level 
during the current financial year 2015-16. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
13.  The Committee notes the reply. 
2015-16 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
14. The Committee notes that the group- wise alloca tion will help the Ministry to 
reallocate funds among the Schemes subsumed within the group, when the need arises. The 
Committee hopes that this financial arrangement would impart more flexibility to the Ministry 
in terms of allocation, leading to optimum utilizat ion of funds. Nevertheless, the Committee 
desires that due care and caution should be exercis ed to ensure that the new scheme of 
allocation does not affect the progress of existing  schemes/ programmes of the Ministry and 
also the functioning of vital Organisations under t he Ministry. The Committee would like to 
emphasize that the interse fund allocation of the g rouped heads should be brought to the 
notice of the Committee at appropriate time.                  
                                                                                                   (Para No. 27 of ibid ) 

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
15. The Ministry has noted the above recommendation  regarding exercise of due care 
and caution to ensure that the progress of existing schemes/ programmes of the Ministry is not 
affected, as also the functioning of vital Organiza tions under the Ministry. The break-up of 
Plan funds allocated for grouped heads will be brou ght to the notice of the Committee at 
appropriate time.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
16.  The Committee notes the reply. 
Ministry’s Projected Demand vis-à-vis  Budgetary allocation 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
17. The Committee is at a loss to note that allocat ions had been reduced in almost all 
sectors, which has adversely impacted Archaeology, Museums, Libraries and other important 
Organizations under the Ministry. Culture imparts i mportant identity to a nation. In the 
development paradigm, culture plays a crucial role in the life of a nation. Therefore, 
preserving, protecting and promoting our rich cultu ral heritage assume greater significance, 
for which the Ministry must get adequate allocation . The Committee is of the firm view that 
with the existing scale of allocation, even the exi sting schemes and activities of the Ministry 
will be difficult to run. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry 
should actively pursue the matter of increasing the  allocation at the RE stage in the current 
financial year, with the Ministry of Finance. 
                                                                                                  (Para No. 31 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
18. The Ministry will actively pursue the matter of  increasing the allocation at RE stage 
2015-16 with Ministry of Finance in respect of the schemes/activities of grouped Plan 
allocation, as per the requirement projected by the  organizations/schemes during the current 
financial year. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
19.  The Committee may be apprised of the outcome there of. 
Non - Plan 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
20. Even the Non- Plan allocation of the Ministry, the Committee believes, does not 
inspire confidence as the success of Plan activitie s largely depends upon the Non- Plan 
activities. Existence of large number of vacancies and lack of adequate manpower at various 
levels particularly in ASI, will certainly adversel y affect the regular upkeep, maintenance, 
protection and preservation of our cultural heritag e. Pace of expenditure in this section, 
Committee hopes would be maintained in future also.      
                  (Para No. 34 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
21. As regard allocation of Non-Plan funds for the Ministry, as against BE (Non-Plan) 
2014-15 of Rs. 676.00 crore which was reduced to Rs . 659.00 crore at RE level 2014-15 due 
to austerity measures, an amount of Rs. 714.00 cror e has been provided to the Ministry under 
Non-Plan during the year 2015-16. Out of Rs. 659.00 crore under Non-Plan at RE 2014-15, an 
expenditure of Rs. 650.43 crore was incurred during  2014-15, which is about 98.70% of RE. 

This Ministry has been making all out efforts for f illing up the large number of vacancies at 
various levels in the cultural organizations. 
  Regular action is being taken to fill the vacanci es in different cadres of 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).  For this pur pose Staff Selection Commission (SSC) 
and Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) have bee n requested regularly. Prompt action 
is also being taken to fill up vacancies through pr omotion.   Department Promotion 
Committee meetings are held regularly by ASI and UP SC for this purpose.   In the last one 
year 144 posts (26 Group ‘A’ + 77 Group ‘B’ + 41 Group ‘C’) and 76 posts (9 Group ‘B’ + 67 
Group ‘C’) were filled up by methods of Promotion a nd Direct Recruitment respectively.  
UPSC has been requested to finalize the selection o f candidates for 32 posts of Dy. 
Superintending Archaeologists through direct recrui tment and to hold DPC for filling up 
another 15 posts of Dy. SA by the method of promoti on. SSC is in the process of selection of 
candidates for filling up 43 posts of Assistant Arc haeologists. The SSC has forwarded the list 
of selected candidates for appointment against 23 v acant posts of Assistant Archaeologist 
Chemist. Further, requisitions for filling up total  number of 1365 posts Multi-Tasking Staff 
(MTS) have been sent to the respective regional offices of SSC. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
22.  The Committee urges the Ministry to pursue activel y the matter of filling up of 
posts without delay, with UPSC and SSC. 
Issues taken up/pending with Ministry of Finance 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
23. The Committee notes that the sums demanded by t he Ministry of Culture are 
required for not only existing schemes, but also fo r new ones declared mid way by the Prime 
Minister as well as Finance Minister. The Committee , therefore, strongly endorses the request 
put forth by the Ministry to the Ministry of Financ e.   The Committee is of the firm view that 
reduced allocation for vital Schemes of the Ministr y would adversely affect the core activities 
of the Ministry, thereby, undermining the mandate of the Ministry.       
                                                                               (Para No. 36 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
24. The Ministry is processing the matter for provi ding additional funds for the 
activities proposed to be carried out, as mentioned  in the FM Budget Speech with Ministry of 
Finance. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
25.  The Committee would like to know the outcome there of. 
Savings/under-utilizations during 2014-15 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
26. The Committee notes that as per the details fur nished by the Ministry, savings 
during 2013-14 was due to varied reasons such as no n-filling up of vacant posts, delay in 
completion of works, postponement of some programmes etc.        
        (Para No. 38 of ibid ) 
27. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry that every possible step should be 
taken to ensure that under- utilization of funds do es not occur. The Committee is of the view 
that periodic monitoring by the Ministry, of the pr ogress of schemes/programmes would help

36. During the last 3 years, the highways sector is  going through a difficult phase. Public Private 
Partnership (PPP) projects through Build Operate Tr ansfer (BOT) (Toll) mode are not able to attract bi ds. 
Major highway developers in the country which are l imited in number have capacity constraints includin g 
over-leveraged financials due to excessive exposure  to infrastructure projects including highways. 
Another inherent issue for the sector is lack of av ailability of debt products aligned with revenue st ream 
profile of highway projects resulting in financial stress in projects during the initial construction years. In 
addition, there have been issues like some banks re aching the ceiling as per sectoral exposure norms. 
Quite a few projects have got stalled in the construction stage due to these reasons. These are discouraging 
prospective bidders to participate in new project bids.  
37. In order to revive the Highways Sector and to e xpedite the implementation of road projects, this 
Ministry has taken following steps: 
(a) With the constant interaction with Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, a number o f 
specific bottlenecks for speedy execution of National Highways Projects have been resolved.  
(b) Three meetings of the Group of Infrastructure h eaded by Hon’ble Minister (RT&H,S) have 
been held and a number of inter-Ministerial issues have been resolved. 
(c)  Government on 13.05.2015 has approved the poli cy which permits 100 % equity divestment 
after two years of construction completion for all BOT projects irrespective of year of award. This wo uld 
facilitate infusion of liquidity in the sector by e nabling existing developers to release their locked -in 
equity in completed projects. Out of the 115 Conces sion Agreements signed up to 30 
th  September, 2009 
on BOT (Toll) and BOT (Annuity), 80 such projects h ave been completed, and the locked in equity of 
such completed projects works out to approximately Rs.4500 crores. This amount of equity by itself 
would be able to support construction of an estimat ed length of around 1500 kms of projects on PPP 
mode. 

(d) Government on 13.05.2015 has also approved the policy for one time fund infusion to revive 
and physically complete languishing BOT projects. F or any languishing highway project in BOT (Toll) 
mode that has achieved at least 50% physical comple tion and it is also established that infusion of 
moderate funding can quickly bring this project to completion, NHAI will provide financial assistance to 
such a project from the overall budget corpus of NH AI on loan basis for a short tenure and with a pre-
determined return.  This assistance (say bridge fun d) will be provided on a loan basis at Bank Rate +2 % 
drawing a parallel with the provisions of the Model  Concession Agreement. This proposal would help 
physical completion of languishing projects bringin g relief thereby, to the citizens /highway users in  the 
area. 
(e)  This Ministry has also adopted a new Hybrid An nuity model for implementation of highway 
projects in order to encourage private sector parti cipation through adequate incentives. The objective  is to 
maximize the quantum of implemented highway project s within available financial resources of the 
Government. As per this model, 40% the Project Cost  is to be provided by the Government as 
‘Construction Support’ to the private developer dur ing the construction period and the balance 60% as 
annuity payments over  the concession period along with interest on outstanding amount to the 
concessionaire. There is separate provision for O&M  payments by the Government to the concessionaire. 
The private party does not have to bear the traffic  risk. All the payments have been inflation indexed  by a 
Price Multiple Index which is a weighted average of WPI and CPI (IW) on 70:30 bases. This mitigates the 
inflation risk for the developer.

Government, to assist in discharge of its functions.  NRSTMA will have the power to do all things that are

objects of the National Transport Authority.

broad framework for the Government both at the Cent ral and the State level, to take measures for
